tagline: Morocco's economic capital on the Atlantic — a marina-anchored coastal city reaching toward Rabat and the surf coast.
summary: Casablanca is Morocco's largest city and economic capital, fronting the Atlantic with a major port, the landmark Hassan II Mosque on the water, and the redeveloped Marina Casablanca and Ain Diab corniche. The Atlantic coast runs north toward the capital Rabat-Salé and south toward the El Jadida and surf-coast resorts. The Atlantic swell makes this a more demanding operating environment than the sheltered Med or Gulf, but the dense urban waterfront, the marina, and the Casablanca–Rabat corridor offer a real foiling commuter-and-leisure opportunity for a fast, stabilised craft.
competitive_landscape: Casablanca has no urban passenger water transport today — the port is commercial and the coast is used for leisure and surfing. The Casablanca–Rabat corridor, one of Morocco's busiest, moves on congested road and a high-speed rail line; the coast itself is unused for mobility. A foiling tier is a greenfield mode here, with the marina and corniche as natural anchors and the Rabat run as a flagship coastal corridor — gated to the conditions the Atlantic allows.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The urban-waterfront and near-coast hops — Marina↔Ain Diab corniche (~2 nm), Casablanca↔Mohammedia (~13 nm) — sit inside the 70 nm all-electric range, suited to clean city rotations off the marina when Atlantic conditions allow.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The flagship Casablanca↔Rabat coastal corridor (~48 nm) on exposed Atlantic water is a Quanta-LR hybrid route (H2 2026+) — the hybrid range and sea-keeping handle the swell and remove charging dependency on the open coast, where an all-electric day-boat would be marginal.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates platform-scale foiling deployment; for Casablanca the emphasis is on the Quanta-LR's sea-keeping to handle Atlantic swell on the flagship Rabat corridor.

regulatory_note: Casablanca maritime activity falls under Morocco's National Ports Agency (ANP) and maritime administration, with the commercial port and the leisure marina under separate management. Morocco's strong coastal-development and clean-energy agenda supports an electric tier; the principal operating consideration is Atlantic-swell gating rather than regulatory complexity, with the marina providing a ready urban anchor.
seasonality: A year-round mild Atlantic climate supports the urban and commuter network, with summer (May–September) the leisure peak; Atlantic swell and winter storm systems are the dominant operating constraint, making the Quanta-LR's sea-keeping and the conditions-gating of the open Rabat corridor essential to reliability.
